title: Protoplanetary Disks in ρ Ophiuchus as Seen from ALMA
question: What are the 870 um dust continuum fluxes and radii of disks in rho Oph, how do they differ between singles, binaries, triples and transition disks and compare with Taurus, and are binary disks tidally truncated?

evidence.quote: Reference key: \[a\] (cite: ra05), \[b\] (cite: du04) , \[c\] (cite: ch15), \[d\] (cite: rr16)

what.value: Taurus comparison sample from Spitzer survey plus literature (sub)mm fluxes

evidence.quote: we used the results of the *Spitzer* survey performed by (cite: re10).

what.value: Transition disk classification from IR colors

evidence.quote: were identified by (cite: ci10) to be candidate transitional disks on the basis of *Spitzer* near-/mid-infrared colors

recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration per configuration, split fields, phase-only selfcal for C34-1, combine, CLEAN (multi-scale for extended)
Gaussian fit in the image plane
assumptions: distance 137 pc to convert to radii

recipe.method: Optically thin isothermal: M = F d^2 / (kappa B(Td))
assumptions: Td = 20 K, kappa = 0.03 cm2/g at 870 um (Hildebrand), gas-to-dust 100:1, d=137 pc

recipe.goal: Compare sub-population flux and radius distributions
recipe.method: Kaplan-Meier estimators with upper limits for flux (detections only for radius) and pairwise log-rank test; significance p<~0.05
key_parameters: 3 sigma map value used as upper limit for non-detections

recipe.method: Same KM method on Taurus sample from Rebull et al. 2010 with 870 um fluxes inferred from spectral index (assume 3 if unavailable)

recipe.goal: Test tidal truncation of binary disks
recipe.method: Pichardo et al. 2005 truncation radius with statistical deprojection of a, e from projected separation, uniform e in [0,1], mass ratio q=1

recipe.goal: Search for gaps via radial profiles
recipe.method: Deproject using fit center, inclination and PA; azimuthally average surface brightness

answer_key.quantity: Singles vs binaries (no circumbinary) flux p-value
Singles Oph vs Taurus flux p-value

evidence.quote: This yields an estimate of $f = 0.122$ with a 95% confidence interval of $0.031 < f < 0.21$.

answer_key.quantity: Gap radii in ROph 9 and ROph 38

evidence.quote: there are obvious deficits of emission observed at approximately 65 and 170 au, respectively.

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN threshold, mask, niter and multiscale scale values
CASA self-calibration solint and reference antenna details
